src/files/infrastructure/uploader/local/files.module.ts: `storage: diskStorage({ destination: './files', ... })` hardcodes local disk persistence. This is infrastructure (persistence) logic.

src/files/infrastructure/uploader/local/files.module.ts: diskStorage `filename` callback builds the stored name with `${randomStringGenerator()}.${file.originalname.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase()}`. This is storage naming logic for the infrastructure layer.
The module's own path (src/files/infrastructure/uploader/local/) also marks it as an infrastructure adapter, even though the layer model classifies it as presentation.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file is declared presentation because it matches **/*.module.ts. A Nest module can fairly act as a composition root that wires infrastructure, so this could be read as framework wiring. But inside the MulterModule.registerAsync useFactory, the file writes three behaviours inline instead of delegating them: (1) a fileFilter that sets which file types may be uploaded (jpg/jpeg/png/gif only) and rejects others with an UnprocessableEntityException. This is an upload policy or business rule, which belongs in the application or domain layer, or in a dedicated validator. (2) diskStorage with a hardcoded destination './files'. This is persistence and storage logic, which belongs in an infrastructure adapter. (3) The diskStorage filename callback, which builds stored file names from randomStringGenerator() and the lower-cased original extension. This is also storage logic for the infrastructure layer. The module also picks the persistence module at load time by calling databaseConfig().isDocumentDatabase. That is acceptable wiring. The inline policy and storage code is not, so the file holds responsibilities from more than one layer.
